title: Turn a page of divs into landmark elements
summary: The header, nav and footer are all divs, so a screen reader cannot jump between them. Replace them with header, nav, main and footer.

files.content:

turns.user: got a support ticket from a screen reader user, says they can only move around our page by headings. can you fix it

assistant.body: Sure. A div with class="header" is just a box to assistive tech. Replacing them with header, nav, main and footer turns each one into a landmark, and screen readers list landmarks so the user can jump straight to one. Note: a page should have only one main. The class attributes stay, so the existing CSS keeps working as expected. A header inside an article, on the other hand, does not become the header of the whole page.

turns.user: done. now they say there are 2 navigations and they cant tell which is which

assistant.body: Good catch. Two landmarks of the same kind are both announced as just "navigation". Give each one a name with aria-label. The screen reader reads the name together with the kind, so a label that says navigation would be announced twice.
